metadata.model: ShadeRoute Evidence-Based Heat-Health Hospital Surge & Resource Readiness Model
metadata.study_area: Bhubaneswar (SOA ITER Campus Catchment & IMS SUM Hospital)
metadata.methodology_note: Central estimates are epidemiology-informed planning assumptions derived from public institutional bed capacities, NCDC NAP-HRI benchmarks, and AIIMS emergency medicine protocols. They provide transparent decision support for resource readiness rather than empirical hospital admissions predictions.

model_grounding.facility_baselines: Derived from publicly established institutional bed counts (IMS & SUM Hospital 1,750 beds, Jagamara UPHC 15 beds, SOA Student Dispensary 8 beds) and standard public health operational capacity estimates, without confidential internal hospital records.
model_grounding.epidemiological_guidelines: Surge multipliers are derived directly from published national clinical guidelines (NCDC NAP-HRI 2024) and peer-reviewed Relative Risk benchmarks (Phung et al. 2016, Bobb et al. 2014, WHO Heat-Health Action Plans).
model_grounding.resource_standards: Dedicated Heat Stroke Unit (HSU) bed need (20%) and emergency IV crystalloid fluids (3.5L/patient) adhere strictly to AIIMS Emergency Medicine and NCDC protocols for transparent scenario planning rather than empirical admissions backtesting.

academic_references.title: Heat–Health Action Plans: Guidance (2nd Edition, 2024)
academic_references.summary: Establishes institutional alert criteria, hydration stations, and documented 10%-25% all-cause emergency visit surge during extreme heat events.
academic_references.apa: World Health Organization. (2024). Heat–health action plans: Guidance (2nd ed.). WHO Press.

academic_references.authority: National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) & MoHFW
academic_references.title: National Action Plan on Heat-Related Illnesses (NAP-HRI, 2024)
academic_references.summary: Standardizes hospital tiered preparedness, dedicated Heat Stroke Units (HSUs), emergency cooling beds, and IHIP heat reporting across Indian facilities.
academic_references.apa: National Centre for Disease Control. (2024). National action plan on heat-related illnesses (NAP-HRI). Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India.

academic_references.title: Standard Clinical Operating Protocols for Emergency Management of Severe Heat-Related Illnesses (2023)
academic_references.summary: Mandates active evaporative/ice-water immersion cooling, aggressive fluid resuscitation guidelines (3.5L/pt), core temperature tracking, and daily surveillance reporting.
academic_references.apa: All India Institute of Medical Sciences. (2023). Standard clinical operating protocols for emergency management of severe heat-related illnesses. AIIMS Emergency Medicine Press.

academic_references.title: Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Heat Wave Forecasting, Warning and Dissemination (2023)
academic_references.summary: Defines Yellow (Watch), Orange (Alert), and Red (Warning) thresholds, departure from normal temperatures, and multi-day duration impacts for Odisha.
academic_references.apa: India Meteorological Department. (2023). Standard operating procedure for heat wave forecasting, warning and dissemination. Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India.

academic_references.title: Ambient Temperature and Risk of Cardiovascular, Respiratory, and Metabolic Hospital Admissions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
academic_references.summary: Pooled relative risk of hospital admissions per heatwave: RR = 1.16 (95% CI: 1.09-1.24), with renal RR = 1.30 and direct heat illness RR = 2.45.
academic_references.apa: Phung, D., Thai, P. K., Guo, Y., Morawska, L., Rutherford, S., & Chu, C. (2016). Ambient temperature and risk of cardiovascular, respiratory, and metabolic hospital admissions: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Environmental Research, 151, 804–814.

academic_references.title: Cause-Specific Risk of Hospital Admission Related to Extreme Heat in Older Adults
academic_references.summary: Demonstrates compounding +35% to +45% emergency surge on consecutive heatwave days due to physiological thermal accumulation and failed nighttime cooling.
academic_references.apa: Bobb, J. F., Obermeyer, Z., Wang, Y., & Dominici, F. (2014). Cause-specific risk of hospital admission related to extreme heat in older adults. JAMA, 312(24), 2659–2667.

soa_student_health_centre.name: SOA ITER Student Health Centre
soa_student_health_centre.eligibility: Available exclusively for ITER students & faculty (free of cost)
soa_student_health_centre.description: On-campus primary dispensary providing free triage, Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT), and vital monitoring. Serious cases are stabilized and transferred via university ambulance to IMS & SUM Hospital.

jagamara_uphc.name: Jagamara UPHC
jagamara_uphc.tier: Level 1: Govt. Urban Primary Health Centre (NHM)
jagamara_uphc.eligibility: Open to all public, neighborhood residents, and outdoor workers
jagamara_uphc.description: Primary public health centre covering the 3 km² neighborhood population; free ORS distribution, outdoor worker heat stress screening, and early heatstroke triage.

astang_ayurveda.name: Astang Ayurveda Hospital & Centre
astang_ayurveda.eligibility: Open to public for outpatient & traditional heat management
astang_ayurveda.description: State Ayurvedic medical institution in Gandamunda; specialized traditional herbal rehydration, cooling therapy, and heat exhaustion recovery within the 3 km² study zone.

sum_hospital.name: IMS & SUM Hospital
sum_hospital.description: Major 1,750-bed teaching hospital of Siksha 'O' Anusandhan; comprehensive ICU, nephrology, cardiology, and dedicated Heat Stroke Unit (HSU) receiving severe transfers.

2026-09-22.clinical_advisory: 🟢 ROUTINE READINESS: Active rainfall and overcast conditions suppress acute solar heat-health presentations. Maintain routine operations.

soa_student_health_centre.capacity_action_command: 🟢 ROUTINE READINESS: Monsoon rainfall and cloud cover suppress acute heat presentations. Maintain routine operations.

direct_heat_illness.label: Direct Heat Illness (Sunstroke, Heat Exhaustion, Syncope)

renal_metabolic.label: Acute Kidney Injury & Dehydration (Azotemia, Electrolyte Loss)

morning_rise.clinical_mechanism: Initial ambient heating; mild exhaustion in early outdoor commuters.
morning_rise.shift_recommendation: Activate ORS corner; pre-cool hydration packs.

peak_danger_window.clinical_mechanism: Peak solar radiation & surface heat; acute sunstroke, hyperthermia, collapse.
peak_danger_window.shift_recommendation: CRITICAL SHIFT: Double triage nurses; pre-cool IV fluids; staff all HSU beds.

delayed_decompensation.clinical_mechanism: Post-exposure dehydration wave; outdoor workers & elderly renal decompensation.
delayed_decompensation.shift_recommendation: Deploy IV rehydration teams; maintain rapid electrolyte blood testing.

nocturnal_residual.clinical_mechanism: Severe residual cardiovascular strain under elevated night temperatures.
nocturnal_residual.shift_recommendation: Monitor admitted inpatient wards for cardiac stability.
